summary: Log fire lookout begun on Chipman Hill in Middlebury, VT, in 1932 by state crews; Forest Lookouts marks it removed with no date; hill is now a town park.

facts.design: Log tower being built by state men to state forestry plans; 1932 plans gave 55 feet with an observation lookout on top
facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts marks the tower removed, with no date given; no source describes what remains on the summit
facts.agency: Vermont state forestry department (plans and state crews, per 1932 newspapers)

access.note: Chipman Hill Park is a town park with hours listed as 6:30am to 9pm; a 2018 town document describes a fenced equipment site on the summit

visit.trail_note: The lookout is listed as removed, so there is no tower to climb; the town park has walking trails

events.note: Construction of a log tower started August 1932 by state men to forestry department plans; Middlebury College supplied logs; completion not documented in the sources
New tool house built near the fire tower, replacing an older building

notes_for_editor: Removal date is not in any source. The 55 ft height and the fire-warden staffing are 1932 plans; no source confirms them. The 2018 Middlebury packet concerns cell and radio towers on the summit and does not name the 1932 lookout, so do not treat that compound as the lookout site. Brief access 'unknown' is superseded by the public town park.
